views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Engage the October Washington round and the working-level meetings without new structural commitments or a further tariff/entity-list spiral. Keep the existing retaliatory architecture in place, use limited farm-purchase authorizations and the 16-category exemption list as reversible goodwill, and press for a matching U.S. delay or rollback of the October 15 hike and December 15 List 4B. Do not lock in large purchase quotas or IP/SOE reforms until the U.S. puts concrete tariff relief on the table.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. Since May the U.S. raised List 3 to 25%, put Huawei and dozens of affiliates on the Entity List (expanded again 21 Aug), designated China a currency manipulator after CNY broke 7, and on 1 Sep put List 4A (~$110–125B) into force at 15%, with List 4B still hanging over phones/laptops/toys (timeline 2019-05-10 through 2019-09-01). That maps to the CHN +0.5 anchor: export sectors hit, Huawei firm-level targeting, FX pressure. Official August activity confirms the bite — industrial output +4.4% YoY, a 17½-year low, with delivered industrial exports down 4.3% (Reuters 16 Sep); PPI in deflation; CPI pushed by a 47% pork spike from African swine fever. DEXCHUS weakened from ~6.71 in April to 7.08 on 18 Sep. Offsetting that, reserves are stable near $3.11T, merchandise exports have not collapsed, and mid-September goodwill (China’s first exemptions 11 Sep; soy/pork exclusions and soybean cargoes 13 Sep; Trump’s two-week delay of the next hike) has reopened a talks path. Escalating now would likely invite the delayed Oct 15 hike and Dec 15 List 4B and deepen the industrial slump; a large unrequited concession would repeat the May collapse over enforcement/structural text. Negotiation with small, reversible agricultural gestures is the stance that matches a +0.45 threat: stop the next tariff wave, buy time on Huawei/tech, and keep structural red lines off the table until there is a matching U.S. offer.
key_factors: List 3 at 25% plus List 4A at 15% already live; List 4B still scheduled for 15 Dec
Huawei Entity List plus August affiliate expansion remains the core tech/sovereignty threat
CNY through 7 and U.S. manipulator designation; reserves still ~$3.11T
August industrial output at a multi-year low and export deliveries falling
Pork/ASF food-price pressure creates a domestic reason to allow some U.S. farm imports
Reciprocal mid-September goodwill and Liu He–Lighthizer October round make talks the live option
Further Chinese escalation would likely trigger the delayed U.S. October hike and December List 4B

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
China announces first tariff-exemption list for some US products (16 categories; industrial inputs / chemicals / related — not a broad farm rollback).
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork, and some other farm goods will be excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
CNY/USD latest 7.0849 on 2019-09-18, +0.377 / +5.6% over the window after breaking 7 on 5 Aug.
China reserves excluding gold latest ~$3.112T (2019-09-01), essentially flat (−0.08%) — FX pressure without a reserve crisis.
China CPI index rose from 107.8 (Apr) to 109.8 (Sep), consistent with food/pork inflation tightening the domestic constraint.
Industrial output growth unexpectedly weakened to 4.4% in August, slowest since February 2002; value of delivered industrial exports fell 4.3% on-year.

China will exclude soybeans, pork and other farm goods from additional tariffs and allow a certain amount of purchases, responding to Trump delaying the next hike from Oct 1 to Oct 15; Liu He set working-level talks then an early-October Washington round.
BIS added 46 additional non-U.S. Huawei affiliates to the Entity List (rule dated 21 Aug 2019), tightening the May listing rather than easing it.
